notes.decision: Translated 'summons.' The lexeme is unidentified in standard glossaries but is structurally the chapter's organizing term ('first/second/third ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ'). Best semantic match in our accumulated vocabulary is the verb ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'summon forth' (the Lycopolitan emanative-vocative verb). 'Summons' captures the active calling-down then calling-up motion described in each instance: the cosmic Call goes out upon a class of beings, draws their substance downward, and brings it back upward. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'depth.' The form is unusual; could be Lyc. ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲍ 'form, structure' (= Sah. ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄), or possibly ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fullness.' 'Depth' best fits the cosmological scenario of Life rising up out of the earth-substance — the ascent-from-below pattern dominant in this kephalaion. Confidence moderate.

Read substantivally: 'is choice (substance) of that place.' ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ as qualitative/substantive of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose, select.' Line 6 then refers back with ⲡⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ 'the chosen' as the referent from which Error is driven out.

Translated 'temples.' Distinguished here from ⲙⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'heavens' (lines 10, 12, 14): ⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ = Lyc. ⲉⲣⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'temples' (plural of ⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'temple'). The structure 'temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens' (lines 13-14) confirms three distinct architectural terms within the heavenly region.

Translated 'array.' From Lyc. ⲥⲉⲡⲧⲉ (= Sah. ⲥⲟⲡⲧⲉ) 'preparation, equipment, ordered arrangement.' Used twice on this page: line 17 'array of those of heaven' and line 28 'the other array of cattle.' Translated consistently as 'array' to preserve the order/equipment register.
Translated 'lies' (qualitative). Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲗ 'spread, lie, sojourn.' The five worlds of flesh 'lie' upon the earth — a stative-cosmological position. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'in likenesses upon likenesses.' Reduplicated construction: ϩⲛ̄- 'in' + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness.' Per terminology rule, ⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered uniformly as 'likeness.' Captures the intensifying-distributive sense that the powers go forth in many varied likenesses.
Translated 'wrath.' Lyc. ⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ = Sah. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'anger, wrath.' Listed with desire (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ) and evil (ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ) as the moral-affective triad of vices.
Translated 'pour down.' Lyc. form related to ϣⲱⲣ 'spread' / ϣⲱⲣϣ̄ 'pour out.' Recurs four times in lines 26-27 of the descending motion: the vices 'pour down' upon men. Confidence moderate.

Read as 3pl future + verb of pouring/sending: 'they shall pour out.' Object follows in line 29: 'the Error and the scourge and the venom.' The verb ϣⲱⲁ likely = ϣⲟⲩⲟ 'pour out, empty.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'scourge.' Coptic ϣⲛϣ 'stroke, blow, scourge' (Crum 569b) fits the toxic-violent register paired with Error and venom. Alternative readings (bond, shame) do not match the inventory of inflicted ills. Confidence moderate.
Translated 'they shall abound.' ϣⲁⲗⲩ- = Lyc. iterative/habitual 3pl prefix, + ⲣ̄-ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'do excess, abound.' Same compound used in line 26 of the vices that 'abound in the powers.'

Translated tentatively 'is fastened ⟨and⟩ ϣⲛⲍ.' ⲉϩⲝ may be a verbal form related to ⲱϩⲝ̄/ϩⲱⲝ 'tighten, fasten, bind' (qualitative or 3pl 'they fasten'). ϣⲛⲍ remains opaque — possible candidates: ϣⲛ̄ⲍ 'examine, visit,' ϣⲏⲛ-ϥ̄ 'his tree,' or ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'sickness.' Left in Coptic in the english field with note. Confidence low.

Treated as 3sg.m perfect prefix: 'he hid' for ⲁϩⲧⲁⲃⲉⲥ. Lyc. ⲁϩ- = standard ⲁϥ- 'he (perfect).' The subject is ambiguous in the lacunose context but most likely refers back to a divine/apostolic agent named in the prior page or in the lacuna at the start of line 1.

Translated 'the powers' (plural). The article ⲧ- is unusual for a plural noun (expected ⲛ̄-), but the verb ⲉⲧⲉϣⲁϩⲥⲱⲟⲩⲍ 'which gather' takes a plural subject and the parallel construction throughout the page is plural. Possibly a Lycopolitan collective form.
